newsitem.title: CYPRUS: CYPRUS TO AUCTION 91-DAY BILLS WORTH UP TO 27 MLN.
newsitem.headline: CYPRUS TO AUCTION 91-DAY BILLS WORTH UP TO 27 MLN.

text.p: The Central Bank of Cyprus will auction up to 27 million pounds worth ($48.75 million) of 91-day treasury bills with an August 13 issue date, the bank said on Friday.
Competitive or non-competitive bids for the issue can be made from August 11 to 9.00 a.m. local (0600 GMT) on August 13, the bank said.

In competitive bidding, bidders set the price at which they are willing to buy the bills. The bid can be accepted in part or in whole only if the price set is equal or higher than the price set for the specific issue by the central bank. The minimum bid is set at 10,000 pounds.
Non-competitive bids are those bids where the bidder expresses his willingness to buy bills at the average price of competitive bids accepted by the central bank. The minimum bid is 1,000 pounds.
